name: a spawn's leftover registers
why: MoonBld's blade (the third kind's 0x69, BN5's code in both) is spawned by 0x080D3398 through the common spawn, which keeps its caller's r1-r4 as the object's words (r1 at +0x10, r3 at +0x3C): MoonBld's attack sets neither (0x080EF9C2-0x080EF9DC), so the blade takes what the attack's own calls left: r1's top byte a byte of a return address into MoonBld's code (BN5's own, BN6's copy's: apart where the copy stands), r3 the attack's own caller's, BN5's RunAIAttack (0x0801857A) MegaMan's AI data, BN6's (0x0801B9E6) the battle state. Its first sweep (0x080D332C) writes its panel over +0x10-+0x13 and MegaMan's place over +0x34-+0x3F, so the words live their first frame alone, read by nothing.
evidence: chip_moonbld1: the blade's +0x3C MegaMan's AI data in BN5's, 0x02034880 in BN6's at t38, its first frame; equal from t39
chip_moonbld1: its +0x13 0x67 in BN5's, 0x97 in BN6's at t38 (+0x34 the same return address in both, BN5's 0x080EF967 and its copy), +0x12 and +0x13 its panel, (3, 2), in both from t39
BN5 0x080D3398: push {r0,r1,r2,r5}; movs r0,#0x69; bl 0x08003178 (the third kind's spawn, r1-r4 its words)
